_provenance: Aggregated from 'Family Survey Results + Insights' (bina Growth, 2026). Two separate surveys, never combined: Survey A = whole-school family survey, n=103, 44% response rate. Survey B = middle-school parent survey, n=108 responses. All figures are aggregates — no individual family or student data appears on this page.
_openQuestions: Survey field dates are not stated in the source deck — page currently says 'our most recent family survey' rather than naming a month. Add `window` once Sophie confirms.

RESOLVED for launch: the 'sense of belonging' section is deliberately written so it holds true whether the survey asked about the parent's or the child's belonging — it never says whose. An earlier draft asserted it was the parents (following the deck's own reading: 'Kids connecting does not equal parent feeling a sense of belonging') but that was unverified, so it was pulled before publishing. If Sophie confirms the question wording, the section can be made more specific and stronger.

NPS benchmark is now sourced to ISM (see `npsBenchmark`). Note what the source does NOT say: it gives no single 'average school NPS' figure, and ISM's own argument is that schools need grade-specific ranges rather than one universal number. The page therefore cites the cross-industry world-class band (70+) and uses ISM's sample sizes as a credibility note — it never claims 'the average school scores X'. Do not add that claim without a source that actually states it.
No parent quotes approved yet. A quotes section is the biggest remaining conversion lever.

The FSI (9.5) is NOT the average of the seven dimensions below — that average is 9.25. It sits right on top of the 'overall satisfaction' score (9.48), so the page describes it as the overall satisfaction measure rather than claiming a formula. Confirm how Sophie calculates FSI.

npsBenchmark.bandNote: Cross-industry NPS bands as cited by ISM: 0–50 good, 50–70 excellent, 70–100 world class.
npsBenchmark.source: Independent School Management (ISM), "Net Promoter Score Surveys: Is My School's Score 'Good'?", Ideas & Perspectives Vol. 47 No. 5, 1 May 2022
npsBenchmark.caveat: ISM's own finding is that schools need grade-by-grade ranges rather than one universal number, and it publishes no single 'average school NPS'. Never write 'the average school scores 50' — the source does not say that.

headline._fsiNote: FSI (9.5) is deliberately NOT used on the page. It is not the mean of the seven dimensions (that is 9.25) and we cannot describe its formula honestly yet, so the page uses the overall satisfaction score (9.48) instead — which needs no explaining and costs 0.02. Reinstate FSI only once Sophie confirms how it is calculated.
